text:
maria_support: Customer report — SSE stream aborts mid-response when they toggle WiFi on iPhone (iOS 16). They see partial tokens then the socket closes with an RST/FIN from client side. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Customer upset because they were billed for 1,024 tokens but only received ~400 tokens in the UI. Repro steps attached, asking for root cause and billing guidance.

sam_eng: Can you paste client logs + the server-side request id and region? Any proxy in front of them?

maria_support: Sent logs from customer (snip). They are on carrier+wifi roaming — switch triggers immediately before stream ends. No client proxy reported. Server side shows: `200 OK` then `connection closed` after ~12s. Region: us-west-2. Attached minimal repro below.

jamie_mobile: Quick note — iOS tends to close sockets aggressively when switching networks. Does their app use background tasks/VOIP? If not, OS may tear down the socket and userland gets FIN.

nate_infra: From infra side, edge proxy (our TLS terminator) has an idle timeout of 60s by default. But this is mid-stream (not idle). Two possibilities: client sends RST/FIN on network change OR NAT rebinding kills the TCP flow. We need a tcpdump around the time. Can we get pcap or `ss` dump from the server?

maria_support: Customer provided a simple tcpdump snippet — shows client's IP change at 14:22:05, then we see a TCP FIN from client at 14:22:06. Server still streaming data until that FIN. Repro steps they followed: 
1) Start SSE request with `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream`
2) Wait for server to emit ~400 tokens (they capture data events)
3) Toggle WiFi off (cellular takes over)
4) Immediately see connection close, client reconnect logic kicks in but stream restarted from scratch.

maria_support: Customer included the following server-side snippet showing last lines: ```
[2024-11-02T14:22:04.921Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d streaming token: "..."
[2024-11-02T14:22:05.103Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d streaming token: "..."
[2024-11-02T14:22:06.012Z] TCP FIN from 203.0.113.45:53422 -> 54.85.10.17:443
[2024-11-02T14:22:06.015Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d stream aborted, client disconnected
```

sam_eng: That looks client-initiated. From our side, tokens already emitted to the socket are considered delivered. Billing rules: tokens emitted by the model before socket tear are billed. If the client disconnected before finalization, we still billed for emitted tokens.

kevin_billing: Confirming: billing is based on model tokens processed/emitted. If the request aborted, charges reflect the work already done. We can open a customer credit request if this looks like a clear client-side network fault and the customer impacted is entitled to a one-off adjustment. Please include request id + full timeline.

maria_support: Customer wants an automated way to resume without paying double. They have logic to reconnect but it restarts generation. Any recommendations to resume partial generation?

jamie_mobile: SSE doesn't have native resume for in-flight text generation. Options: 
- Client implements local buffering + retry that requests next tokens with a deterministic seed/prompt (if model supports continuation)
- Use chunked checkpoints: ask our API to emit interim checkpoints (e.g., provide partial output + an id to resume) — not currently supported as a generic feature.

nate_infra: Operational mitigation: we can add an early keepalive/heartbeat event from server to reduce chance of mid-gen perceived idle, but that doesn't prevent a client-side FIN on network change. Recommend improving client reconnection UX: if they reconnect quickly, check for idempotency keys on server to continue or detect duplicate billing. For now, engineering can explore a resume token feature.

sam_eng: Action items: 
- @nate_infra: collect tcpdump and confirm no proxy reset (we need full 30s around event).
- @jamie_mobile: add a short doc blurb with recommended client reconnection pattern for iOS (exponential backoff, avoid silent restart that recharges model cost).
- @kevin_billing: offer to triage billing credit on a case-by-case basis; ask support to gather timeline.

ops-bot: Escalation created -> ENG-SRE #tickets/78921 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/TICK-78921) :rotating_light:

maria_support: FYI forwarded customer a temporary workaround: increase client-side socket persistence (where possible), and implement a small client-side checkpoint save so re-requesting can start from last saved chunk, not from scratch. They accepted temporary credit review.

sam_eng: For triage notes: if we want to avoid repeated billing on flaky networks, a longer-term product idea is a `resume_id` param so servers can persist partial outputs tied to a request (short TTL) — customers could reconnect and request continuation. Adding to roadmap backlog.

kevin_billing: I'll stand by to review credits once support posts logs + token counts. Provide `req_0a1b2c3d` and approximate token counts from server logs.

maria_support: Uploaded customer pcap and server logs to the ticket, included token count math. Customer emailed happy with the temporary credit path and OSS-style client reconnection guidance. Closing loop here, marking as monitored for similar reports. :white_check_mark:

nate_infra: Leaving a final note — for mobile handoffs we see two typical patterns: immediate FIN (client kills socket) or long orphaned half-open connections (NAT timeout). This one is the immediate FIN case; mitigation is mostly client-side. We'll keep an eye for patterns and export sample NAT traces into the ticket.

sam_eng: Thanks team. If we get multiple customers hitting this, let's prioritize a small resume-ticket design spike.

maria_support: Closing thread, will follow up if customer reports recurrence.
